::: {#exr-geometric}
## The geometric series

::: {.lm-solution}
1. Multiplying the sum $s_n$ by $1 - q$, all terms but the first and the last cancel: $(1 - q) s_n = 1 - q^{n+1}$.

1. For $|q| < 1$, $q^{n+1} \to 0$, so $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} q^k = 1 / (1 - q)$. With $q = 1/10$:
   $$
     \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 9 \cdot 10^{-k} = \frac{9}{10} \cdot \frac{1}{1 - 1/10} = 1.
   $$
:::
:::

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import math
```

::: {#exr-alternating}
## The alternating harmonic series

### Implementation

::: {.lm-solution}
```{python}
def partial_sums(n):
    s = 0.0
    sums = []
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        s += (-1) ** (k + 1) / k
        sums.append(s)
    return sums
```
:::

### Errors

::: {.lm-solution}
```{python}
sums = partial_sums(1000)
for n in [10, 100, 1000]:
    print(n, abs(sums[n - 1] - math.log(2)))
```

The error is about $1 / (2n)$: one more correct digit needs ten times as many terms. The geometric series with $q = 1/10$ gains one digit with each term.
:::
:::
